answer: Sybil resistance arises because each bonded identity is independently escrowed, while correlated equivocation among k identities triggers a quadratic penalty, O(k^2), through joint evidence and slashing. A coordinated swarm therefore cannot multiply influence cheaply: upon detection, an exponential multiplier in capital loss applies to the colluding set, rapidly exhausting collateral through asymmetric depreciation. Whether identities gather at a wharf, canyon, or shale site is irrelevant; only verifiable behavior matters.
